html:
The Tuscarora War was fought in North Carolina from 1711 to 1715 between English colonists and the Tuscarora and their allies.

Settlers were pushing into Tuscarora land along the coastal rivers, among them Swiss and German colonists who founded New Bern in 1710. Traders cheated the Tuscarora, and slave raiders took their people. In September 1711 the southern Tuscarora and their allies, among them the Pamlico and the Coree, attacked farms along the Neuse and Pamlico rivers and killed well over a hundred settlers.

North Carolina was weak, so South Carolina sent two armies made up mostly of Native allies, above all the Yamasee. In March 1713 the second army stormed the Tuscarora fort of Neoheroka. Hundreds were killed, and hundreds more were sold into slavery. The northern Tuscarora under Tom Blount stayed out of the war and kept a small reservation.

The war broke Tuscarora power in the south and opened the interior of North Carolina to settlers. Many Tuscarora went north to the Haudenosaunee, who took them in as the Sixth Nation around 1722; their descendants are the Tuscarora of New York. Neighbouring peoples such as the Meherrin were also squeezed. Soon after, the Yamasee themselves rose against South Carolina.
sum: The Tuscarora War was fought in North Carolina from 1711 to 1715 between English colonists and the Tuscarora and their allies.
